newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ salary and wage rate growth up in yr to Dec qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ salary and wage rate growth up in yr to Dec qtr.

text.p: Salary and wage rates (including overtime) were 2.0 percent higher in the December 1996 quarter than in the December 1995 quarter, the Labour Cost Index released by Statistics New Zealand on Friday shows.
"The 2.0 percent increase is slightly higher than that of the 1.9 percent for the years to December 1995, March, June and September 1996," SNZ said.
It said an increase of 0.7 percent in the December quarter from the September quarter, the largest quarterly rise since the 0.8 percent rise in the March 1991 quarter, contributed to the annual rise.
Base salary and ordinary time wage rates being paid to employees in all sectors were on average 2.0 percent higher in the December 1996 quarter than in the December 1995 quarter.
SNZ said this increase was the same as that for the years to March, June and September 1996, but higher than those of 1.5 percent and 1.9 percent for the years to September and December 1995.

Overtime wage rates increased by 0.7 percent in the December 1996 quarter and rose 2.0 percent from the December 1995 quarter to the December 1996 quarter, matching the annual increase in salary and ordinary wage rates for the first time.
SNZ said annual growth in salary and wage rates continued to slow in the private sector, but gather pace in the public sector.

Salary and wage rates being paid in the private sector increased by 1.8 percent in the year to December 1996, following increases of 2.0 percent and 1.9 percent in the years to June and September 1996.
"By comparison, the latest annual increase for the public sector, at 2.5 percent, follows increases of 1.9 percent and 2.2 percent for the years to June and September 1996," SNZ said.
Salary and wage rate increases were recorded for all nine major occupation groups from the December 1995 quarter to the December 1996 quarter.

SNZ said the highest increases were for professionals, up 3.0 percent, and trades workers, up 2.2 percent. The smallest increases were 1.1 percent for agriculture and fishery workers, and 1.6 percent for clerks.
SNZ said 50 percent of salary and ordinary time wage rates did not change from the December 1995 quarter to the December 1996 quarter.

"About three in five of the rates which increased rose by more than two percent but not more than five percent. The average rise was 3.8 percent, up from 3.6 percent for the year to December 1995," it said.
The median increase in the year to December 1996 was 3.0 percent, up from 2.8 percent for the year to December 1995.
